text:
1	# Architecture - notes
2	
3	A fourth kind of design, besides features, the design system and the shell:
4	**the project's architecture**, kept as markdown files that agents read and
5	shown to the team on the project's Architecture pages, the way the design
6	system's gallery shows the system. Prelude's own architecture (from
7	`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plan.md`) is the sample data.
8	
9	This design is those pages: views at Prelude's own URLs
10	(`/f/:folder/architecture/…`), with states shaped as Prelude's model of the
11	files would be.
12	
13	## Decided (2026-10-22, with the person)
14	
15	- **A design of `"kind": "architecture"`, one per project** (R-p0j), like the
16	  system and the shell. Its sessions shape it ("draft it from the code").
17	- **Prelude reads the files itself**, as it reads RULES.md, so nothing is
18	  written twice (D-e8y in the sample). The real architecture design will
19	  have no states; this design's states stand in for what Prelude reads.
20	- **Markdown, a file per thing**, in the design's `architecture/` folder (as
21	  the system's is `system/`):
22	  - `overview.md`: a summary, the layers in order, the principles (title, why);
23	  - `parts/<id>.md`: a header (title, layer, kind: module / process / outside,
24	    `files` globs, `uses` part ids), then sections: Responsible for, Not its
25	    job, Owns;
26	  - `decisions/<id>.md`: a header (title, status, date, parts, supersedes),
27	    then Context, Decision, Consequences. Ids are `D-` + three random
28	    characters, so branches never clash;
29	  - `flows/<id>.md`: a title, a summary, numbered steps each starting with
30	    the part's id.
31	  Prelude prepares what's derived: each part's "used by", decisions and
32	  findings, and the map's layers.
33	- **Proposed decisions are accepted by merging** (R-7tq): an agent's
34	  proposal is reviewed with its branch, and Prelude marks it accepted at
35	  merge (as it clears a route's `from`).
36	- **Agents use it** (R-c2m, R-h9w): ever

1	# Rules: Architecture
2	
3	- **R-p0j.** A project has one architecture at most, as it has one design system and one app shell.
4	  *proposed*
5	- **R-c2m.** Every design, build and fix agent reads the architecture's principles, and the parts its change reaches, before it changes anything.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture*
7	  *proposed*
8	- **R-h9w.** An agent whose change would go against the architecture proposes a decision on its branch, rather than making the change without saying so.
9	  *proposed*
10	- **R-7tq.** A proposed decision is accepted when the branch that proposed it is merged into main, and agents on other branches don't see it before then.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/decisions/:decision*
12	  *proposed*
13	- **R-4vx.** After every turn that changes code, the changed files are checked against the architecture, and a build or fix agent is told what doesn't match with its next message.
14	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture @ drifted*
15	  *proposed*
16	- **R-k5e.** A part may use the parts its file says it may, in its own layer or below it; any other use is reported, and so is a file no part names or a named file that isn't there.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/parts/:part @ drifted*
18	  *proposed*
19	- **R-w8d.** Decisions are listed newest first.
20	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/architecture/decisions*
21	  *proposed*

text:
1	# Prelude
2	
3	A tool for designing (and later building) apps with an agent: pick a folder,
4	chat with an agent, watch the design appear. The plan, its ground rules and
5	every decision taken are in `docs/plan.md`. Read it before adding a feature.
6	Nothing gets added until we've decided where it fits in the simple model
7	(folder, design, session, screen; a chat surface and a design surface).
8	
9	## Koda
10	
11	This application is built with Koda. Before writing or changing a view, a
12	stylesheet or a handler, load the matching skill - `koda-app-authoring`,
13	`koda-styling`, `koda-server-setup` (and `koda-composition` for anything that
14	crosses an application or a host) - and follow it. Look attributes up in the
15	Koda reference (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md`, the version
16	Prelude depends on) rather than from memory. Run `koda-review` before calling a
17	change finished.
18	
19	Koda is the npm package `@kodalang/core`, pinned in `package.json`, and it ships
20	its skills. The ones in `.claude/skills/` are copies of the installed package's;
21	`test/skills.test.js` fails when they differ. After upgrading Koda, run
22	`npm run skills` to copy them again, and read what changed.
23	
24	## Working here
25	
26	- `npm start` runs Prelude on http://localhost:4200 (`PORT` to change it).
27	  Views are cached when the server starts: restart it after changing one.
28	- `npm test` runs the tests (node --test). Add tests for what you build.
29	- The desktop app: `npm run build:shell` builds `tauri/src-tauri` (about 10
30	  minutes from cold) into `dist-shell/Prelude.exe`. `npm run test:shell` runs its
31	  Rust tests. The app is a window on the server: it uses one already answering
32	  `/health` on localhost:4200 (`npm start`), or else starts `node start.js`
33	  itself (Prelude's folder is found above the exe, or `--root`/`PRELUDE_ROOT`;
34	  its output goes to `~/.prelude/server.log`) and stops it on quit. `--server
35	  <url>` or `PRELUDE_URL` p

2	//
3	// One turn runs at a time per design, whichever of the design's sessions it
4	// belongs to, so two sessions never write the same files at once. Every event

9	// The agent's words stream as they're written: a "live" entry is pushed when a

I've built the Architecture overview, its check region and the decision list into Prelude, and made R-c2m, R-4vx, R-p0j and R-h9w true. I couldn't run anything, so neither the tests nor the build have run yet; Prelude's render of every state after this turn is the first real check.

**Pages**
- The four views are in `server/views/architecture/`, copied element for element. That's the overview, `_check`, `_decisions` and the `_decision-item` partial they share. The design had no styles of its own to move, and the map component is already in the design system.
- `server/architecture.js` builds the model from the architecture design's markdown files. It reads the overview, parts, decisions and flows, and works out what's derived: "used by", each part's decisions and findings, and the layers on the map. The model's types are written from the states' shape, so all three states fit it.
- `main.js` answers the three URLs with the page or a fragment. The decision list filters by `?q=` and `?status=`.
- `routes.json` points the three routes at the app's views.

**Rules**
- **R-c2m:** design, build and fix prompts now tell the agent to read the overview and the files of the parts its change reaches before changing anything. This also covers the app, layouts and connect builds.
- **R-h9w:** the same instructions say to propose a decision on the branch rather than drift. Design sessions can now write in the architecture's folder so they can do that.
- **R-4vx:** after each build or fix turn on a branch, Prelude checks the code files the turn changed. It reads JavaScript and TypeScript imports only, so far. Findings show as a note in the chat, are added to the agent's next message, and update the project's check.
- **R-p0j:** "architecture" is now a kind of design, like the design system and the shell, so a project can't have a second one.
- The `architecture-checked` event is sent down the app's live channel, so the open check card reloads.
- I removed the four *proposed* lines from RULES.md. R-7tq, R-k5e and R-w8d stay proposed, though decisions are already listed newest first.

**What to look at before approving and opening the pull request**
1. **The markdown format.** The design didn't specify how each file is laid out, so I chose one: a `key: value` header after the title, then `##` sections. The agent that drafts the architecture is told the same format. It's written up in NOTES.md.
2. **Which files the check expects to belong to a part.** It's files under a folder a part's glob names, plus files next to a file a part names (not in subfolders). Folders no part names, like `test/`, aren't reported. If that rule is wrong, the "belongs to no part" findings will be wrong too.
3. **A change outside this design.** The New design modal (`projects/_new-design.eta`, from the project landing page design) now handles `?kind=architecture`, which the empty page's "Draft it from the code…" link needs. None of that design's states use it, so its approved screens shouldn't change.
4. **The check isn't saved.** It's kept in memory and runs again when the folder's commit moves. After a restart, the first page view runs it fresh.

The part, decision, flow and Decisions pages aren't built yet. I added `test/architecture.test.js` and notes in CLAUDE.md, and an open question in NOTES.md: the architecture design's own page has nothing to show beside the chat.
